accepted_concepts: not to be understood from the outside

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the unreadable into the open
confuses being unreadable with being dishonest

inscrutable.mental_hook: Nothing shows, and nothing can be guessed.
inscrutable.semantic_hint: The word for a face that reveals nothing at the card table.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses lacking feeling with the near-twin about being knocked out

insensate.required_nuance: without feeling, whether sensation or compassion
insensate.semantic_hint: The word for violence described as blind and unfeeling.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses being unaware with the near-twin about being unfeeling

insensible.required_nuance: unaware, or below the threshold of notice
insensible.semantic_hint: The word for someone knocked out cold, and for change too slow to see.

accepted_concepts: harmful in a gradual hidden way
doing harm before it is detected

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the hidden into the plain

insidious.required_nuance: harm that works unseen until it is far advanced
insidious.mental_hook: By the time you see it, it is late.
insidious.semantic_hint: The word for a disease that does its damage before any symptom appears.

accepted_concepts: edge into a position by degrees

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts a sly hint into a plain declaration
confuses the speaker's hinting with the listener's deducing

insinuate.required_nuance: suggesting without saying, or easing in unnoticed
insinuate.mental_hook: Never says it. You still heard it.
insinuate.semantic_hint: What a remark does when it implies dishonesty without alleging it.

accepted_concepts: flat to the taste or the mind
insipid.required_nuance: without flavour or interest, in food or in art
insipid.mental_hook: No flavour, in food or in prose.
insipid.semantic_hint: The word for soup with nothing in it and a novel with nothing in it.

accepted_concepts: refuse to give way on it

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts standing firm into giving way

insist.mental_hook: Says it again, and will not drop it.
insist.semantic_hint: What someone does by repeating a demand until it is met.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses rudeness with the near-twin about bankruptcy

insolence.semantic_hint: The word for a shrug given to a direct order from a superior.

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses rudeness with the near-twin about bankruptcy

insolent.required_nuance: disrespect, shown openly and with contempt
insolent.semantic_hint: The word for a reply that treats a superior with open contempt.

accepted_concepts: without the funds to meet obligations
owing more than one can pay

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses bankruptcy with the near-twin about rudeness

insolvent.mental_hook: Cannot pay. The near-twin is merely rude.
insolvent.semantic_hint: The word for a company that can no longer meet its debts.

insouciance.required_nuance: unconcern worn lightly, almost with style
insouciance.mental_hook: Not worried, and rather stylish about it.
insouciance.semantic_hint: The word for a shrug at bad news delivered with perfect calm.

accepted_concepts: fill someone with the urge to do something
give rise to a feeling in someone
inspire.mental_hook: Breathes it into them, which is the Latin.
inspire.semantic_hint: What a great teacher does to a student's ambition.

accepted_concepts: an example of a general thing

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts one case into the whole class

instance.required_nuance: one particular case of a general thing
instance.semantic_hint: The word for a single example offered to illustrate a pattern.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the noun sense for the tested verb

institute.required_nuance: setting something up or starting it formally
institute.semantic_hint: What a company does when it starts legal proceedings.

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the intolerable into the agreeable
reads the root as the person not suffering

insufferable.semantic_hint: The word for someone unbearably pleased with themselves.

insular.required_nuance: narrow because cut off, like an island
insular.semantic_hint: The word for a village that takes no interest in anywhere else.

insularity.required_nuance: the narrowness that comes of being cut off
insularity.mental_hook: The island, as a state of mind.
insularity.semantic_hint: The word for a profession that reads only its own journals.

accepted_concepts: someone taking up arms against a government
a member of an armed rising

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the rebel into the supporter of authority

insurgent.semantic_hint: The word for a fighter in an armed revolt against a government.

accepted_concepts: a rising to overthrow a government
insurrection.semantic_hint: The charge brought after an armed attempt to overthrow a government.

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts the comprehensible into the obscure
confuses being understandable with being intelligent

intelligible.required_nuance: capable of being understood, not necessarily clever
intelligible.mental_hook: Can be understood. Says nothing about clever.
intelligible.semantic_hint: The word for speech clear enough to follow over a bad line.
